'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**[[2021 Uganda bombings]]
***It is revealed that yesterday's explosion on a bus in [[Mpigi District]] was carried out by an [[Allied Democratic Forces|ADF]] [[suicide bombing|suicide bomber]]. The attacker was killed, and three other people were injured. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211026-uganda-bus-blast-a-suicide-bomb-attack-police (France 24)] [https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/dead-passenger-in-mpigi-bus-explosion-was-terrorist-says-museveni-3596510?view=htmlamp (Daily Monitor)]
*[[Islamic State insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|Islamic State insurgency in Iraq]]
**[[Islamic State]] [[militant]]s attack a village in [[Diyala Governorate]], [[Iraq]], killing 11 people and injuring several others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/27/isil-attack-iraqi-village-kills-11 (Al Jazeera)]
*Aftermath of the [[2016 Berlin truck attack]]
**A man who was critically injured in the [[Vehicle-ramming attack|truck attack]] in [[Berlin]], [[Germany]], in 2016, dies from complications related to his injuries this month, becoming the thirteenth fatality of the attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-59048891 (BBC News)]
*Aftermath of the [[October 2021 Sudanese coup d'état]]
**[[Sudanese Armed Forces|Military]] leader [[Abdel Fattah al-Burhan]] says that he and his forces seized power in an attempt to avoid a [[civil war]] in [[Sudan]], saying that "the dangers we witnessed last week could have led the country into civil war". Meanwhile, anti-coup protests occur across the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/telecommunications-interrupted-sudan-after-coup-2021-10-26/ (Reuters)]
**Deposed [[Prime Minister of Sudan|prime minister]] [[Abdalla Hamdok]] and his wife are released by the military. However, several [[Government of Sudan|government]] officials continue to be detained and face trial. [https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/sudan-pms-office-says-he-has-been-brought-home-1.1635284992141 (AFP via ''Gulf News'')]
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbas]]
**[[Ukraine]] confirms it has carried out its first [[drone strike]]s using the [[Turkey|Turkish]]-made [[Bayraktar TB2]], destroying a [[Russian separatist forces in Donbas|pro-Russian separatist]] [[122 mm howitzer 2A18 (D-30)|D-30 howitzer]]. A [[Ukrainian Ground Forces|Ukrainian soldier]] is killed and another wounded by rebel artillery near [[Hranitne, Volnovakha Raion|Hranitne]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]]. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/10/27/ukraine-destroys-pro-russian-artillery-in-its-first-use-of-turkish-drones-a75420 (''The Moscow Times'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Imperial House of Japan]]
**[[Princess]] [[Mako Komuro|Mako of Akishino]] marries [[commoner]] Kei Komuro, thereby nullifying her imperial title under [[Imperial Household Law|Japanese law]] and becoming [[Mako Komuro]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211026-japan-s-princess-mako-marries-after-years-of-controversy (AFP via France 24)]

'''Business and economy'''
*A [[cyberattack]] affects [[gas station]]s across [[Iran]], rendering [[government of Iran|government]]-issued electronic cards used to buy subsidized fuel unuseable and leaving motorists stranded in long queues. No group immediately claims responsibility for the attack. Iran blames an "unidentified foreign power" as being behind the attack. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/cyberattack-hits-iranian-gas-stations-nation-80786605 (ABC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Two people are killed and another is missing as [[flood]]s triggered by a powerful storm is affecting [[Catania]], [[Sicily]], [[Italy]]. Roads have been completely submerged in parts of the region. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-59048809 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]]
****[[Belgium]] reintroduces the usage of [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face mask]]s at public places and will expanding the usage of COVID Safe Ticket to bars, restaurants, and fitness club beginning next week amid a rise of [[COVID-19]] cases and hospitalizations. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-europe-health-shootings-pandemics-5f80af212a90f1a52a4f90094f5fb120 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****[[Bulgaria]] reports a record 5,863 new cases and 243 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 575,306 and the nationwide death toll to 23,316. [http://www.bta.bg/en/c/DF/id/2503928 (Bulgarian News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 1,106 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 232,775. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/10/26/russias-covid-deaths-hit-new-record-high-ahead-of-nationwide-restrictions-a75411 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Switzerland]]
****[[Switzerland]] recommends that people aged above 65 years old receive the [[booster dose]] of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] and should be done at least six months after they received their second dose. The booster dose for that age group will begin in mid-November. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/switzerland-recommends-covid-19-booster-shots-people-over-65-2021-10-26/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 734 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 64,936. [https://www.rferl.org/amp/ukraine-covid-record-deaths/31529744.html (RFE/RL)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain]]
****[[Bahrain]] approves the usage of the [[Sinopharm BIBP COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 3 and 11 years old. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/coronavirus/covid-19-bahrain-approves-sinopharm-vaccine-for-children-aged-3-11 (''Khaleej Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****The city of [[Lanzhou]] is placed under lockdown due to a cluster of COVID-19 cases. The city, which has a population of over four million, accounts for roughly a fifth of new cases reported in [[China]] since October 17. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/china-puts-lanzhou-city-of-4-million-under-covid-lockdown-2588084 (NDTV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]]
****[[British Columbia]] announces that beginning from January 2022, the province will offering a [[booster dose]] of either the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer]] or [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] vaccine to people aged above 12 years old who have already received their second dose, becoming the first jurisdiction in [[North America]] to do so. [https://vancouversun.com/news/local-news/covid-19-b-c-plans-to-offer-booster-shots-to-all-british-columbians (''Vancouver Sun'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***The [[African Union]] will purchase 110 million doses of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] in a deal brokered by the [[United States]], which will defer delivery of some doses intended for the U.S. in order to facilitate the deal. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/26/african-union-to-buy-up-to-110-million-moderna-covid-19-vaccines (Al Jazeera)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis]], [[Belarus–Poland relations]]
**[[Poland]] increases the number of [[Polish Army|soldiers]] [[Military deployment|deploy]]ed on its [[Belarus–Poland border|border]] with [[Belarus]] from 6,000 to "about 10,000" in order to prevent the flow of further illegal crossings by [[Middle East|Middle Eastern]] migrants being flown in by the [[Belarusian government]]. The troop surge comes after two border guards were hospitalized over the weekend after a group of 70 migrants stormed a section of the border. [https://euobserver.com/tickers/153338 (''EUObserver'')]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**The [[ASEAN Summit]] takes place virtually without the participation of [[Myanmar]], following the [[ASEAN|bloc]]'s decision to disinvite the country's [[State Administration Council|military junta]] chief [[Min Aung Hlaing]] for refusing to cooperate on a [[peace process]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20211026-asean-summit-opens-without-snubbed-myanmar-junta-chief (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro]], [[2021 Brazilian protests]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
**A Senate committee approves a resolution to gain access to [[President of Brazil|Brazilian President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]]'s internet activity. The Senate also votes today on whether to indict Bolsonaro with multiple charges, including charges accusing him of mismanagement of the pandemic, [[charlatanism]] and [[crimes against humanity]]. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-crime-caribbean-health-brazil-80823c6b0d77567d5912373f9d756cbe (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil-senators-call-records-bolsonaros-internet-activity-2021-10-26/ (Reuters)]
*At least 150 people are arrested by [[Europe]]an and [[United States|U.S.]] authorities during a joint crackdown on traders of drugs, weapons and other illicit goods on [[darknet]] [[e-commerce]] sites. The majority of those arrested are from [[Germany]], the U.S. and the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://apnews.com/article/technology-europe-arrests-drug-trafficking-101b78b631e0899a5f78c4e886644dea (AP)]
